paper: Cullen, Wang & Culcer 2025, arXiv:2509.20436v3 (Orbital Hall effect in spin-3/2 hole-doped semiconductors)
system: Bulk p-type Ge, 4x4 spherical Luttinger model

open_questions.question: Build the dominant quantum correction Delta j1 (interband-polarization / dipole-rotation term of Eq. 6) and check whether it alone lifts the conventional ~49 toward the ~10^3 headline.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The paper's whole thesis is that quantum corrections DOMINATE the OHE; Delta j1 (and Delta j2) are named as the two largest contributions (Fig. 2, lines 590-591). Without them the ~20x gap to the headline cannot close, and 'orbitronic promise of Ge' rests entirely on this unbuilt physics. This is the single most important missing piece.
open_questions.next_step: Implement the covariant-derivative form of the interband OAM current from the modern theory of orbital magnetisation (Eq. 6 first term, all velocity + off-diagonal OAM elements). Reuse the existing spherical eigenbasis kernel in work/ohe_spherical.py; add the interband-dipole matrix elements. Validate order-of-magnitude against paper Fig. 2 sigma-component curves.

open_questions.question: Build Delta j2 (interband OAM matrix elements / time-fluctuating OAM) and Delta j3 ([r,v] non-commutativity, opposite sign) and reconstruct the full signed sum sigma_L + sigma_conv + Delta sigma_1,2,3.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Delta j3 has OPPOSITE sign to all other contributions (line 522), so the total is a signed cancellation, not a simple sum. Getting the net ~10^3 requires all terms with correct relative signs; a partial build could give a spuriously wrong magnitude. Tests whether our conventional piece has the right sign relative to the corrections.
open_questions.next_step: Extend the kernel with the L-operator interband matrix elements and the position-velocity commutator term; assemble the signed total and compare each component's magnitude/sign to Fig. 2 (sigma_L, sigma_conv, Delta sigma_1, Delta sigma_2, Delta sigma_3 curves for Ge).

open_questions.question: Does the full (non-spherical) 4x4 and the 6x6 LKBP Hamiltonian change the Ge number materially, and is it required for the other four semiconductors (Si especially)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The paper uses the spherical 4x4 only for analytic insight and switches to full 4x4 / 6x6 for numerical accuracy; Si REQUIRES 6x6 (small delta_so ~40 meV, large gamma2-gamma3 difference). Our spherical Ge number cannot be extended to Si without the 6x6, and cubic anisotropy (gamma2 != gamma3) may shift even the Ge value.
open_questions.next_step: Implement Eq. (1) full 6x6 with material-specific gamma1,gamma2,gamma3,delta_so from the paper's Table I; rerun the Kubo integration for Ge (check vs spherical) then Si/GaAs/InAs/InSb.

open_questions.question: Is the community-standard Go-et-al conventional-Kubo convention we used numerically identical to the paper's 'proper' current (Eq. 7 analogue with the tilde/check non-degenerate/degenerate matrix-element split)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: For spin-3/2 holes the OAM is not conserved, so the proper vs conventional current distinction (which the paper stresses for the SHE, lines 555-558) can differ by O(1) factors or more. If our sigma_conv ~49 is computed in a slightly different convention than the paper's sigma_conv curve, even the 'conventional agreement' claim needs a convention audit.
open_questions.next_step: Derive the proper orbital current from Eq. (7) with L replacing s, implement the degenerate-manifold (check) vs non-degenerate (tilde) Berry-connection split explicitly, and compare to our braced-anticommutator conventional form at identical params.

open_questions.question: How do the OHE (and the dominant quantum corrections) scale with Fermi energy / hole density, and does the predicted ~10^3 survive at experimentally accessible densities?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Our conventional piece already drops from 49 (EF=10 meV) to 34 (EF=5 meV) -- a strong density dependence. The paper's orbitronic proposal for Ge is only useful if the large OHE persists at realistic p-type doping; the EF-dependence of the DOMINANT quantum-correction terms is the experimentally decisive curve.
open_questions.next_step: Once Delta j1,2,3 are built, sweep EF (or hole density n) across the paper's stated range (up to ~10 meV) and reproduce the total sigma_OHE(EF) trend; compare to the paper's density-dependence figure and to the YIG/W/Ge, YIG/Pt/Ge experimental order of magnitude (Ref. 62).

next_steps: Implement Delta j1 (interband-polarization term) first -- highest leverage on closing the ~20x headline gap.
Add Delta j2 and Delta j3 with correct relative signs; assemble the full signed sigma_OHE total for Ge and compare component-by-component to Fig. 2.
Promote the model from spherical 4x4 to full 4x4 then 6x6 (Table I params) to cover Si and check Ge cubic-anisotropy shift.
Audit the conventional-vs-proper current convention (Eq. 7 tilde/check split) so the sigma_conv comparison is apples-to-apples.
Sweep Fermi energy / hole density to reproduce the sigma_OHE(EF) trend and confront experiment (Ref. 62).
